message.content:
Thirty-eight bucks, used, no box, and a faint smell like somebody else's basement. I knew what I was signing up for. Mostly.

The space bar rattles. Not dramatically, but every time I hit it there's this little tin-can shiver that makes me think a screw is loose somewhere. (I checked. No screws are loose. It's just the stabilizer being a jerk.) And the "L" key occasionally repeats itself, so sometimes I send emails that say "hellllo" with all the confidence of a man who doesn't proofread. It happens maybe once an hour. Annoying, not fatal.

Here's the thing, though: my hands like it. I write a lot of long, dull emails, the kind with bullet points and apologies, and after two hours on this thing my wrists feel fine. The key travel is deep and a little springy, and the typing sound is a soft, low thock rather than a clack. Pleasant.

I asked the seller what switches were inside. He answered a week later. A week! By then I'd already guessed browns, and he said "browns," so, thanks, I guess.

Returning it would've meant a box, tape, a trip to the post office. I kept it. Honestly, I'd probably buy it again, rattle and all.
